in_text_mentions: Small nodules, most of which were calcified, were observed in nine (39.1%) patients (Figure 4). These nodules were the only finding in one case. Peripheral reticular opacities associated with small calcified nodules were observed in five (21.7%) patients (Figure 5). Ground-glass opacities without centrilobular ground-glass nodular opacity were also found in five (21.7%) patients. Calcification in the vessels of the chest wall was seen in four (17.4%) cases (Figure 6) and pleural effusion was observed in five (21.7%) patients.

in_text_mentions: HRCT findings are summarized in Table 1. The main HRCT pattern, found in 14 (60.9%) patients, was centrilobular ground-glass nodular opacities (Figure 1). Punctate calcification within nodular opacities was observed in 6 (42.6%) of these 14 patients (Figure 2). In the remaining eight (57.1%) cases, the ground-glass nodules showed no calcification. In nine (31.9%) patients, centrilobular ground-glass nodules were the only imaging finding.

in_text_mentions: ient's chest radiograph showed increased vascular markings and reticulonodular opacifications (see Figure 1). Computed tomography (CT) scans of chest also revealed diffuse ground-glass nodular opacities, with numerous poorly defined nodules measuring 3–10 mm in diameter both (see Figure 2). The patient underwent a Technetium (Tc) 99 bone scan, which revealed diffuse activity in the lung with significant lighting up of the pulmonary parenchyma, consistent with metastatic pulmonary calcification (see Figure 3).

in_text_mentions: d non-specific bilateral opacities (Figure 1). CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening (Figure 2). panels.rationale: The PET-CT image clearly shows diffuse, intense radiotracer uptake in the bilateral lung fields. The caption explicitly states this finding supports the diagnosis of metastatic pulmonary calcification in the setting of severe mineral imbalance.

panels.figure_caption: PET-CT of the chest demonstrating diffuse increased radiotracer uptake within bilateral lung fields, corresponding to ground-glass opacities This finding, in the setting of severe mineral imbalance, supports the diagnosis of metastatic pulmonary calcification rather than an infection or malignancy.
in_text_mentions: d non-specific bilateral opacities (Figure 1). CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening (Figure 2). Bronchoscopy was unremarkable, and both microbiological cultures and Pneumocystis PCR were negative. Persistent pulmonary changes despite antibiotics prompted nuclear medicine imaging. Bone scintigraphy demonstrated intense tracer uptake corresponding to the pulmonary opacities (Figures 3, 4), as well as uptake in the pancreas, sacroiliac joints, pubic tubercle, and left humerus (suggestive of a possible brown tumour) [3].

Coronal lung window images obtained during the current admission (B) with interval progression of diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: The panel shows a CT scan with a high-attenuation consolidation in the right upper lobe, consistent with the diagnosis of metastatic pulmonary calcification described in the caption and article title. B: The panel shows a CT scan demonstrating high-attenuation consolidation in the right upper lobe (consistent with metastatic pulmonary calcification) and bilateral ground-glass opacities, which is a known complication or associated finding. C: The panel uses a mediastinal window CT to highlight the intrinsic high attenuation and calcification of the pulmonary lesion, confirming the features of metastatic pulmonary calcification. D: The panel uses a mediastinal window CT to highlight the intrinsic high attenuation and calcification of the pulmonary lesion, confirming the features of metastatic pulmonary calcification.
panels.attribution_text: Chuang and Liou. Metastatic pulmonary calcification mimicking refractory pneumonia in an end stage renal disease patient: A diagnostic pitfall.. Radiology case reports 2026. doi:10.1016/j.radcr.2026.07.019. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Serial contrast chest computed tomography demonstrating metastatic pulmonary calcification. (A and B) Coronal lung window images obtained 3 months before the current admission (A) and during the current admission (B) demonstrate persistent high-attenuation consolidation in the right upper lobe with interval progression of diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities. (C and D) Corresponding mediastinal window images better demonstrate the intrinsic high attenuation of the pulmonary lesions, making the calcific nature of the consolidation more conspicuous than on lung window images.
